method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a right triangle ABC with the right-angle marker at C, AC drawn vertical and BC drawn horizontal, so AB is the hypotenuse and AC is the side opposite angle B. From the text, use AC = 1, BC = 2, and ∠C = 90°. Apply the Pythagorean theorem to get AB = sqrt(AC^2 + BC^2) = sqrt(1^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(5). Then use the sine definition in a right triangle: sin B = opposite/hypotenuse = AC/AB = 1/sqrt(5) = sqrt(5)/5.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a right triangle with angle B at the left, BC as the leg adjacent to angle B, AC as the leg opposite angle B, and the right angle at C. From the text, AC = 1 and BC = 2. Compute tan B = opposite/adjacent = AC/BC = 1/2. Then convert tangent to sine using sin B = tan B / sqrt(1 + tan^2 B), valid for an acute angle in a right triangle. Thus sin B = (1/2)/sqrt(1 + 1/4) = (1/2)/(sqrt(5)/2) = 1/sqrt(5) = sqrt(5)/5.
